hard_case: Measured defect (#7695): ripr reported the related test's oracle `assert!(ready && matches!(check(5), Ok(_)))` as exact_value / strong, because any `matches!` text in an `&&` chain credited the whole condition whatever its pattern. RIPR-SPEC-0231 rule 3 (example 7 is the same `Ok(_)` pattern as the whole condition): the `Ok(_)` conjunct only checks the side and `ready` pins nothing, so the chain reads no stronger than `assert!(ready)`, relational_check / weak. The line verdict stays gap; the overclaim showed in the related test's reported oracle. Since #7695's fix ripr reports relational_check / weak.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: check(5) returns Ok(6); Ok(_) accepts it

reasoning: assert!(ready && matches!(check(5), Ok(_))) with ready = true only checks the Ok side: Ok(x + 1) passes, Err(E::Bad) fails. No conjunct pins the value.
